detail: Barry Clough; July 2014. Website upload path 2019 is not publication year. Pages 2 and 4 blank, not OCR failures.
Site assessment precedes strategy; no blanket suitability of every mudflat. Giesen 2007 and Clough 2013 cited for intertidal zonation; not independent support from this manual.

claim: Conceptual diagram: elevation, slope, tidal amplitude, flooding, drainage, propagule dispersal, soil composition/compaction/moisture/salinity
detail: All nodes retained. Mechanistic assessment checklist, not weighted model. No slope direction inferred from slope affecting drainage. Flooding frequency not duration; generic composition is not USDA class/HSG. Propagule transport conditional on tidal access, not distance threshold.

claim: Compacted hard dry clay impedes roots, especially Rhizophora
detail: Practice-wide impediment plus species sensitivity retained; compaction absent from canonical ontology. Do not substitute soil texture class, bulk density or species-independent clay exclusion.

Hard cracked soil/crab holes, standing water/canopy, stilt roots/pneumatophores/lenticels, channelled surface, buried roots, canal tree lines, embankments, mudbanks, stepped shoreline. Photographs illustrate diagnoses, not numeric responses. All indicators considered jointly; absence can have several causes.
Local surface heating mechanism; not mean annual air temperature or global thermal threshold.
Sesuvium is saltmarsh indicator, not mangrove taxon; absence has multiple causes. No mangrove pH exclusion.

claim: Natural regeneration and tidal propagule transport
detail: Rare flooding limits transport at higher sites; daily low-site flooding can prevent settling. No universal increasing flooding direction; Avicennia pioneering-stage context preserved.

Rehabilitation can require protection and sediment deposition. No conversion of native mudflat approved; coastal erosion is not interchangeable with hillslope erosion variable. Stability, erosion and accretion checklist rows retained; no calibrated rates.

ev_mr_elevation_clough14_20261028; local MSL datum only, non-monotonic direction. Local maximum tidal range about 4.3 m, peaks about 2.1 m are site descriptors, not bounds. Full 12×5 monthly table in flooding_table.json. No numerical response curve; no percentages from days/month.

MSL benchmark required; conventional GPS insufficient in source. Tube/dye gauges, at least 10 gauges for 1–2 ha plus two references, protect against waves, proposed channel cuts require site judgement. Equipment dimensions and sample density are not suitability thresholds. Methods illustrations not digitised as evidence.

ESi=HGp−HSi; tide gauge error about 5 cm; recommend three days one month apart. Main text accuracy ±2–3 days/month vs annex 3–4 days/month; interannual difference up to 10 days/month. Station/site tide equality unverified, river flows affect station heights. Do not treat these as validated accuracy or portable model.

Three diagrams: sloping sites, dike-enclosed flat land, shrimp pond embankments. Direction depends on topology/barriers and supply; no monotonic slope or ordinal_1_7 drainage curve. Generic soil texture/structure/compaction/burrows control permeability; no USDA/HSG class mapping supplied.

Hardness/compaction/texture; moisture; salinity; water table top 2–3m on high rarely flooded sites. Low/mid flooding at least 10–15 days/month permits any-season sampling; high sites sample March–May stress. These are sampling instructions, not exclusion thresholds; water-table depth differs from mean-lowest canonical statistic.

claim: Soil coring, pH/Eh, laboratory water/salinity procedures
detail: D-corer/syringe/refractometer from English et al. 1997. Depths 40–50cm or 50cm pit and sample handling are protocols. pH/Eh measureability is not suitability use. Soil water formula printed 100×(FWo−DWo) without mass denominator: dimensionally incomplete; do not implement or silently repair. Salinity formula retained as source method, not executed; ±2‰ claimed precision unvalidated here. Balance specifications differ 0.1g versus <=10mg. Nutrient chemistry explicitly beyond scope.
Rooting depth seldom >1m; dig 1–1.2m to observe water/moisture. Earlier top 2–3m criterion differs. Snapshot presence/depth not mean-lowest groundwater depth; no global rooting cutoff.

12 graphical rows retained in species_salinity_inventory.json including combined Avicennia row. Local project experience; approximate endpoints, no printed values, favourable conditions permit outside ranges. Not EC, family-wide envelope, fitted optimum or independently validated mortality limit.

No single indicator sufficient; document site variation. Monitor survival/growth at least five years. Clough 2013, Giesen 2007 and English et al. 1997 followups retained, not newly acquired or extracted.

General satellite features: tree lines/canopies/drainage/canals/sea proximity. Poor surface drainage: pooled water, canopy, roots/lenticels, pneumatophores, sticky soil. Poor subsurface drainage: hard/cracked/sticky soil, no burrows/sand/shells. Infrequent flooding: hard soil, poor mangroves, Sesuvium, no burrows. Followups: barriers/channels, porous layer/salinity/water table to 1m, quantitative tides. No row is a calibrated exclusion.

Overall stability: offshore clay banks. Erosion: stepped shoreline/tree collapse/boundary drop/no recruitment/eroding channels. Accretion: soft mud/natural regeneration. Indicators explicitly site-specific and variable; no quantitative response.

claim: Tidebase Access database and spreadsheet workflow
detail: Documentation reviewed; .mdb/.xls not acquired or run. Names Tidal_Database, TidebaseApp, TidebaseData, GanhHaoTidalRecords vary. Four tables TidalData/TidalData-Serial/TideGauges/Output and three forms documented. pp30 says 2010–2012 records; p34 says 2010–2013 plus 2011–2014 predictions. Test-data/screenshots not calibration evidence. No approved dataset intake adapter; executable/database followup remains open.
